bottleneck.description: Sole European prime for Vega-C small/medium launch and solid-rocket-motor propulsion (P120C boosters shared with Ariane 6), positioning Avio as the only ESA-funded sovereign small-launch and tactical solid-propellant capability in Europe.

dependency.key_customers: European Space Agency, EU Commission (Galileo, Copernicus), Italian MoD, ArianeGroup (P120C boosters for Ariane 6), defense ministries (European + US tactical missile propulsion)
dependency.key_suppliers: Europropulsion JV (with ArianeGroup) for solid motors, Italian/European aerospace supply chain, Snecma/Safran for upper-stage engines, Italian government-backed CDP financing

editorial.notes: Avio benefits from sovereign-launch policy: ESA has formally designated it as Vega launch service provider post-Arianespace split, and P120C solid boosters are dual-use for Ariane 6 and Vega-C, making it structurally embedded in European institutional access to space. It is also Europe's only tier-1 large solid-propellant prime, relevant for the K-defense-style European missile build-out. However, ESA's European Launcher Challenge (Isar Aerospace, RFA, Maiaspace, Orbex, PLD Space) is funded specifically to introduce competition, and SpaceX rideshare remains a commercial substitute for non-sovereign payloads. Regional monopoly with eroding moat = MEDIUM.
